question: Which ISRO centers participate in International Geosphere-Biosphere programme?

options.text: ISRO Headquarters, Space Applications Centre, National Remote Sensing Centre, Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre
Space Physics Laboratory, National Remote Sensing Centre, Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, Physical Research Laboratory
Physical Research Laboratory, Space Applications Centre, Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, ISRO Satellite Centre
Space Application Centre (SAC), Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, Space Applications Centre, National Remote Sensing Centre

solution:
The correct answer is __**Space Application Centre (SAC), Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, Space Applications Centre, National Remote Sensing Centre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme (IGBP) is a global scientific initiative to study Earth’s environment and the impact of human activities.
 
• Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) actively participates in IGBP through its dedicated research centers.
 
• **Space Applications Centre (SAC)**, Ahmedabad, contributes by providing satellite data for geosphere and biosphere studies.
 
• **Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS)**, Dehradun, specializes in remote sensing technology and its application in environmental studies.
 
• **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)**, Hyderabad, provides geospatial data for climate change and ecological research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme (IGBP):**

 
 
• Launched in 1987, focuses on studying the interactions between the geosphere, biosphere, and human systems.
 
• It provides critical insights into global environmental changes and sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Remote Sensing:**
 
 
• Remote sensing involves acquiring information about Earth’s surface using satellite or aerial platforms.
 
• It is essential for monitoring environmental changes, deforestation, urbanization, and climate impacts.
 
 
 
• **Role of SAC:**
 
 
• SAC develops payloads and applications for Earth observation satellites that assist in environmental studies.
 
• Its contributions include data on vegetation, land use, and atmospheric studies.
 
 
 
• **Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS):**
 
 
• IIRS focuses on capacity building in remote sensing and GIS technologies.
 
• It offers training programs and conducts research on natural resource management.
 
 
 
• **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC):**
 
 
• NRSC operates under ISRO and provides satellite data for environmental and disaster management.
 
• It plays a crucial role in national-level studies on climate change and sustainable development.
